law_text: If the driver of a vehicle intends to turn at an intersection and: The turn is a right turn, both the approach for the right turn and the right turn must be made from the right turn lane if the highway has a right turn lane as set forth in subsection 4 of NRS 484B.223 [NRS-484B-223-4a, NRS-484B-223-4b], or must be made from the extreme right lane.

witness_review.branch: Right-turn lane at a terminating-road intersection.
required_context: An identified driver physically controls a conventional motor vehicle and intends the right turn.
Establish connected terminating and through roads, the lane's governed extent and a feasible receiving route.
Establish public-highway and non-alley intersection facts.
Identify the physically controlling driver and included vehicle; establish public-highway and non-alley intersection status.
Preserve the unresolved NRS 484B.223(4) qualification and the conditional extreme-right-lane alternative without selecting legal phase or occupancy thresholds.
Specify terminating and through-road geometry, the lane's designation and governed extent, and the connected receiving route; observe both approach and turn.
witness_review.reason: A terminating-road intersection can support the intended right turn through its designated right-turn lane.
